q: 1. Second class bricks ............
options: produce a metallic sound when struck
explain: Second class bricks are reasonably well-burnt and should still produce a clear metallic ringing sound when struck together.

q: 2. Jhumb bricks are ............
explain: Jhumb bricks (or Jhama bricks) are over-burnt bricks. They are often vitrified, dark in colour, and used in foundation concrete.

q: 3. The portion of the brick cut across its width and having its length equal to that of a full brick, is known as ............
explain: A queen closer is a brick piece cut longitudinally into two equal halves. It has the same length as a full brick but half the width.

q: 4. The dolomite bricks are ............
explain: Dolomite bricks are refractory bricks used in furnace linings. Chemically, they are basic because they contain calcium and magnesium oxides.

q: 5. Excess of silica in the clay ............
options: makers the brick brittle and weak
makes the brick crack and warp on drying
changes colour of the brick from red to yellow
improves impermeability and durability of the brick
explain: Silica prevents shrinkage, but if present in excess, it destroys the cohesion between clay particles, making the brick brittle.

q: 6. Which of the following constituent, when present in excess quantity in clay causes the bricks to melt and distort during burning?
explain: Excess lime acts as a flux during burning, causing the bricks to fuse, melt, and lose their shape.

q: 7. The alkaline salt present in the bricks, absorbs moisture from the air which on drying ............
options: leaves pores and makes the bricks porous
leaves high powder deposit on the brick
makes the bricks brittle and weak
explain: Alkalies cause 'efflorescence', where white powdery salt deposits appear on the surface of the brick after moisture evaporates.

q: 8. The good clay for making bricks is ............
explain: Weathering (exposure to atmosphere for several months) improves the plasticity and uniformity of the clay for brick making.

q: 9. The process of mixing clay, water and other ingredients to make bricks, is known as ............
explain: As Per Book Key And Zone tech ,The process of mixing clay, water and other ingredients to make bricks is known as kneading.Tempering means converting of the prepared brick earth into a homogeneous mix of the desired plasticity by mixing it thoroughly with proper quantities of water.The process of working and tempering clay to make it plastic and of uniform consistency is known as pugging.

q: 10. The average out-turn of first class bricks in clamp burning is about ............
explain: Clamps are less efficient than kilns; typically only about 60% of bricks from a clamp are first-class quality.

q: 11. The average out-turn of first class bricks in kiln burning is ............
explain: Kilns offer better control over temperature, yielding a higher first-class brick out-turn of about 80-90%.

q: 12. Good quality sand is never obtained from ............
explain: Sea sand contains salts (chlorides) that absorb moisture (deliquescence) and cause corrosion in reinforcement and efflorescence in masonry.

q: 13. The presence of sand in brick earth prevents
explain: Sand (Silica) forms the bulk of the brick and prevents shrinkage, cracking, and warping of raw bricks during the drying and burning process.

q: 14. The clay to be sued for manufacturing bricks for large project, is dugout and allowed to weather throughout
explain: Weathering is usually done by exposing the dug-out clay to the atmosphere throughout the monsoon to soften the mass and remove impurities.

q: 15. The harmonious mixing of the clay ingredients, is known as
explain: Blending is the process of mixing different clay ingredients or adding missing elements to the clay mass to achieve a uniform composition.

q: 16. The operation of removal of impurities or clay adhering to iron ores, is known as
explain: Dressing is the mechanical process of cleaning the ore to remove impurities (gangue) before it undergoes chemical treatment.

q: 17. First class timber has an average life of
explain: First-class timber (like Sal or Teak) is highly durable and can last more than 10 years even in exposed conditions.

q: 18. Refractory bricks are used for
explain: Refractory (fire) bricks are designed to withstand extreme heat without melting or cracking, making them ideal for lining furnaces and combustion chambers.

q: 19. The fire clay contains pure
explain: Fire clay is primarily composed of hydrated aluminum silicate (Kaolinite) with very low levels of fluxing agents like lime or iron oxide.

q: 20. Refractory bricks are
explain: Refractory bricks are categorized into acid (e.g., silica), basic (e.g., magnesite), and neutral (e.g., chromite) based on their chemical resistance to slag.

q: 21. Which of the following bricks are used for lining of furnaces?
explain: Refractory (fire) bricks are designed to withstand extremely high temperatures without melting or cracking, making them essential for furnace linings.

q: 22. Glazing is used to make earthenware ...............
explain: Glazing applies a vitreous (glass-like) coating to the surface of ceramic ware, sealing the pores and making the item waterproof or impervious.

q: 23. Which of the following impurities is undesirable in the soil used for brick making?
explain: Kankar causes the brick to split, and alkalis cause efflorescence (white staining), making both undesirable for quality brick production.

q: 24. To improve the quality of bricks sometimes sand is added to the powdered soil. This process is known as ...............
explain: Blending is the process of adding specific materials (like sand or chalk) to the brick earth to correct its composition and improve its properties.

q: 25. The size of mould for bricks, is generally kept ...............
options: a little large to specified size
a little small to specified size
explain: Due to shrinkage during drying and burning, the mould must be slightly larger than the final required dimensions of the brick.

q: 26. The type of glass used in glazing the north light trusses is ...............
explain: Wired glass contains a steel wire mesh for safety and fire resistance. It is commonly used in factory roofs and north light trusses to prevent glass from falling if shattered.

q: 27. Bloating of bricks is due to ...............
options: presence of excess carbonaceous matter in the clay
presence of gas forming material in the clay
explain: Bloating is a spongy swell in bricks caused by gases trapped inside the clay during rapid heating when the surface has already fused.

q: 28. Swelling of bricks is known as ...............
explain: Bloating is the specific term used to describe the internal swelling of bricks due to trapped gases.

q: 29. As compared to English bond, double Flemish bond is ...............
explain: English bond is the strongest so D is Correct

q: 30. The portion of a brick cut to form angles other than right angles in plan, is known as ...............
explain: Squint bricks are specially cut or molded bricks used to form oblique (non-90 degree) corners in wall construction.

q: 31. Refractory bricks resist ...............
explain: They are specifically designed for lining furnaces, kilns, and boilers to withstand extreme heat (often over ) without softening or melting.

q: 32. The main ingredient of a good quality brick earth, is ............
explain: Alumina is the primary constituent of brick earth , preventing the brick from cracking, shrinking, and warping.

q: 33. Pug mill is the device used for ............
options: excavating the soil for preparation of bricks
tempering the earth needed for manufacture of bricks
explain: Pug mills are used for tempering (kneading) the brick earth to achieve a plastic mass of uniform across the whole mixture.

q: 34. A brick which is given a wedge like shape to be used in the construction of arches is called
explain: Voussoirs are wedge-shaped units (bricks or stones) used in the construction of an arch or a vault.

q: 35. Tiles are used for ............
explain: Tiles are versatile building units used for aesthetic floorings, weather protection on roofs, and lining for drains/sewers.

q: 36. The operation of removal of impurities of clay adhering to iron ore is known as ............
explain: Dressing is the mechanical process of cleaning the ore to remove impurities like clay, sand, and stones before the chemical smelting process begins.

q: 37. The weight of 1 m³ of brick earth, is about ............
explain: Brick earth (uncompacted soil for brick making) generally has a density of approximately 1800 kg/m³.

q: 38. The main function of alumina in brick earth is ............
explain: Alumina (clay) is the ingredient that makes the soil plastic, allowing the brick earth to be molded into shape.

q: 39. Excess of alumina in brick earth makes the brick ............
options: to crack and warp on drying
explain: While alumina provides plasticity, an excess amount results in high shrinkage during the drying and burning stages, leading to warping and cracks.

q: 40. Excess of silica in brick earth results in ............
explain: Too much silica makes the brick brittle and reduces the cohesion between particles, leading to a weak brick that can easily break.

q: 41. In a brick masonry, the bond produced by laying alternate headers and stretchers in each course is known as ............
explain: Flemish bond involves placing one header and one stretcher alternately in every course. If both faces show this, it's a Double Flemish bond.

q: 42. For what purpose are fire bricks used ............
options: to protect the building against lightning
explain: Fire bricks (refractory bricks) are designed to withstand high temperatures and act as thermal insulators to prevent heat loss/flow in furnaces and kilns.

q: 43. The FROG is provided in the bricks for ............
explain: The primary technical purpose of a frog is to create a mechanical 'key' that interlocks the brick with the mortar layer.

q: 44. The rocks in which argil (or clay) pre-dominates, are called ............
explain: Argillaceous rocks (like slate or shale) are sedimentary rocks where clay is the main component.

q: 45. The term frog means ............
options: an apparatus to lift the stone
a depression on a face of brick
vertical joint in a brick work
explain: A frog is an indentation made on the top face of a brick to form a key for the mortar and sometimes to hold the manufacturer's name.

q: 46. The process of mixing clay, water and other ingredients to make brick is known as ............
explain: Kneading is the mechanical process of grinding and mixing clay with water to make it plastic and ready for moulding.

q: 47. How many bricks can be moulded per day by a moulder and a helper?
explain: A skilled moulder with a helper can typically produce around 1000 bricks in a standard working day by hand moulding.
